newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian foreign minister seeks July ASEAN entry.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian foreign minister seeks July ASEAN entry.

text.p: Ung Huot, nominated to become Cambodia's First Prime Minister, has asked ASEAN to admit the strife-torn nation to the regional grouping at its annual foreign ministers' meeting next week.

The Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) postponed Cambodia's entry to the grouping indefinitely last week in response to Hun Sen's ousting on July 6 of his coalition partner, First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh.

Ung Huot, in letters to the seven ASEAN foreign ministers, copies of which were released by his ministry on Friday, said Cambodia was now politically stable and should be admitted to ASEAN at their meeting in Kuala Lumpur on July 23 as earlier planned.

"I firmly hope to meet your kind consideration to admit the Kingdom of Cambodia as a member of ASEAN on 23 July, 1997, as (had) been decided at the Special Meeting of ASEAN foreign ministers on 31 May 1997," the letter said.

Ung Huot, who is also foreign minister, told his counterparts that members of Ranariddh's FUNCINPEC party and Second Prime Minister Hun Sen's Cambodian People's Party agreed to nominate him first prime minister, replacing the ousted prince.
The nomination was approved by Hun Sen's party but the United States has refused to recognise it, saying there was not evidence that Ung Huot's selection was made on a free and fair basis.
Hun Sen on Friday shrugged off mounting international efforts to solve his country's political crisis and told foreigners, including ASEAN, to stay out of his affairs.
He said he would meet three ASEAN envoys on Saturday, but appeared weary of their diplomatic efforts.
"If they don't let us join ASEAN, we won't join. If we don't join ASEAN, it won't be the death of us," he said.
ASEAN said last week it still recognised Ranariddh as first prime minister.
Three of the group's foreign ministers have been holding talks on Cambodia's problems this week.

Indonesian Foreign Minister Ali Alatas, Prachuab Chaiyasarn of Thailand and Domingo Siazon of the Philippines met King Norodom Sihanouk, Ranariddh's father, in Beijing on Thursday and were due to meet Ranariddh in Bangkok on Friday.
The three were scheduled to travel to Phnom Penh on Saturday for talks with Hun Sen and Ung Huot.

Ung Huot in his letter assured ASEAN members that Cambodia's constitution and coalition government remained intact, that the country adhered to the principles of democracy and pluralism and international agreements, and the government remained committed to free and fair elections in May 1998.
ASEAN groups Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam. Burma and Laos will become full members next week.
Some diplomats in Phnom Penh expected Cambodia would be admitted by the end of the year.
